messages:
Tara: sales routed a request from a large prospect (NeptuneHealth) — they want reserved-capacity credits to automatically cover burst traffic and for overages to be billed at a predictable blended per-token rate instead of standard PAYG. can we triage feasibility + launch criteria?
Omar: customer is NeptuneHealth (SaaS, PHI). RFP asks: reserved credits act as a burst pool, blended rate for overage. timeline: they need pricing confirmation in ~3 weeks. case id #78942.
Li: attaching usage notes from support case: steady ~30k tokens/day, weekly spikes to ~1.2M tokens for 2–6 hours. spikes cause 429s once burst pool exhausted. customer wants no failed requests during spikes.
Jessica: finance POV: blended rate means discount vs PAYG. proposing to model a pilot blended at ~0.6 * PAYG initially. need: expected commit size, projected percent of tokens in bursts to estimate revenue impact.
Anita (eng-pricing): current billing separates reserved vs PAYG at invoice time. supporting a shared credit pool + blended repricing requires changes to the metering and repricing pipeline and ledger. rough minimal eng effort: 3–6w for backend changes + 1w QA if no DB migrations; full productization larger. also need audit trail for PHI customers.
dev-billing-bot: sim example: 1M burst tokens @ PAYG $0.0003 = $300. blended@0.6 = $180. delta = -$120.
Tara: to push into product backlog we need: 1) concrete customer doc from sales (commit size, burst cadence, SLA), 2) finance-approved pilot pricing band, 3) eng high-level design + acceptance criteria, 4) security/compliance checklist for PHI. can sales provide doc by EOD Thu?
Omar: will send RFP excerpt + commit numbers by tomorrow morning. quick ask: can product approve a manual pilot (no eng changes) while we scope full feature?
Tara: two paths: manual pilot vs product feature.
- Manual pilot: sales invoices negotiated blended rate; finance issues one-off credit adjustments. Pros: fastest. Cons: manual recon, operational overhead, risk of billing confusion. needs finance signoff and a short contract amendment.
- Product feature: build credit-pool + blended-rate logic in billing runtime + console/API. Pros: automated and repeatable. Cons: requires engineering time, rollout plan, monitoring.
Jessica: finance suggests threshold for manual pilot: minimum $50k ARR. below that, use standard reserved + PAYG overage. manual pilot requires finance ticket and contract amendment.
Anita: if manual pilot chosen, eng still needs to enable meter-exception tagging for reconciliation (2–3 days). full productization estimate = ~6–8 sprints across billing + console + api + QA.
Li: ops note — manual pilots historically cause support friction. if manual route taken, need a one-pager for support with example invoice flows and a named billing contact.
Tara: decision rule for this thread: approve a manual pilot for NeptuneHealth if ARR >= $50k and contract signed by EOM. Next actions and owners:
- Omar (owner): send RFP + expected commit numbers — due: tomorrow 09:00
- Jessica (owner): propose pilot price band & invoice template — due: Tue EOD
- Anita (owner): estimate meter-exception tagging work + runbook — due: Tue EOD
- Li (owner): prepare support one-pager/FAQ — due: Wed
- Tara (owner): file product-backlog ticket for full feature with acceptance criteria — due: Thu
Draft acceptance criteria for product feature ticket:
- Policy: define credit-pool semantics (scope: org/org+projects, expiry, transferable?) and API/console UX
- Billing: config for blended-rate per SKU, ledger changes, immutable audit trail per invoice
- Runtime: seamless fallback when credits exhausted (no 429s), metrics for credit usage and failures
- Telemetry: token-level attribution and cost-delta dashboards for customers and internal finance
- Compliance: invoice export and audit hooks suitable for PHI customers; KMS/HSM references for keys
- Rollout: pilot with 2 customers behind feature flag, canary region, observability & rollback plan
Omar: acknowledged. pushing for ARR number. NeptuneHealth pushed RFP deadline to next month but still tight.
Tara: thanks. I'll log this thread and create the backlog ticket once commit numbers arrive. keeping thread open for updates. :seedling:
